Governors
A Governing Body consists of a group of people from the local community, from all walks of life, who bring with them different viewpoints, experiences, knowledge, skills and ideas. They may be parents, staff at the school, local residents or representatives of local businesses, who work together as a team, with the Headteacher and the leadership team to ensure that the school provides their pupils with the best possible education - and constantly strives to improve.
Governing Body Mission
To provide a happy, friendly, caring and stimulating environment where children grow in self-esteem and achieve their full potential, by:
Elected governors serve a four-year term of office, which can be renewed after this period. The Chair of Governors is elected annually. Any parent having a child in school is eligible for nomination as a Parent Governors.

pageCache.pageTitle: Valley Road Primary School - Information for new parents
pageCache.text:
Information for new parents
Starting primary school is an exciting milestone for both children and their families, and we work closely with parents to ensure that the transition to Valley Road is a positive and reassuring experience.
Once your child has been offered a place, we provide opportunities for families to become familiar with the school before the start of term. These may include visits to the classroom, opportunities to meet staff and information sessions for parents.
During the first weeks of school, we focus on helping children feel settled, confident and happy in their new environment. Our staff take time to get to know each child as an individual and support them as they build friendships and become familiar with school routines.
Communication with parents is very important to us. We keep families informed through regular updates, newsletters and meetings, and we encourage parents to speak to staff whenever they have questions or concerns.
If you would like to visit the school or learn more about joining Valley Road, please contact the school office and we will be happy to help.
You will be shown around by the Headteacher and the visit lasts for half an hour. If you have any questions he will be happy to answer them.
We look forward to meeting you!
Information for new parents

SEND
Valley Road School is committed to improving outcomes and having high expectations for all children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).
We believe that every child is unique and that all pupils should have access to a broad and balanced curriculum that enables them to develop academically, socially and emotionally.
Our most recent Ofsted inspection recognised the inclusive approach at Valley Road, noting that leaders do not use a label as a reason for lowering ambition and that pupils with SEND are supported to learn the curriculum well.
Staff work closely with parents, outside agencies and the school’s SENDCo to ensure that appropriate support is in place for pupils with additional needs. Further information about our SEND provision, including the SEN Information Report, can be found in the documents below.
We understand that for parents of children with SEND, there can be many difficult paths to navigate. Sometimes it can be hard to know or find the answers but we strive to ensure that there is always somebody here to talk through your worries, concerns or queries with.
If additional specialist advice or support is necessary we will work with external agencies ie, The NHS, educational psychologists and play therapists. We believe that a multi-disciplinary approach should be taken to ensure that we meet the pupils' special educational needs.
SEND Coordinator: Mrs Redrup

pageCache.pageTitle: Valley Road Primary School - Activities and clubs
pageCache.text:
Activities and clubs
A wide range of clubs and activities are available at Valley Road to enrich pupils’ learning beyond the classroom.
These activities give children the opportunity to explore new interests, develop skills and build friendships with pupils from other year groups. Clubs vary throughout the year and may include sports, creative activities and other interests depending on staff and external providers.
Participation in clubs helps pupils build confidence, teamwork and independence, and is an important part of school life at Valley Road.
Further information about current clubs and how to sign up is shared with parents during the school year.
There is something for everyone! We welcome ideas and input from parents and other members of the community.
Wraparound Care
Valley Road offers wraparound care to support families who need childcare before or after the school day.
Our Breakfast Club is run by Valley Road staff and operates each morning from 8.00am to 8.50am. It provides a relaxed and welcoming start to the day where children can enjoy breakfast and social time with friends before lessons begin.
Bookings can be made in advance, or parents can book on an ad hoc basis, either in advance or by arriving on the day.
Our after school provision is delivered by Get Active Sports, a well-established organisation that has been running breakfast, after school and holiday clubs across the local area for over 20 years.
Get Active Sports offers a wide range of fun, active sessions for children after the school day. Bookings are made through their easy-to-use online booking system, allowing parents to reserve places either in advance or on the day where spaces are available.
They also operate a staffed office until 6.30pm each weekday, so parents can contact them directly if they require assistance with bookings or have any questions.
Activities and clubs

Curriculum
At Valley Road Primary School we aim to provide a broad, balanced and engaging curriculum that inspires children to develop curiosity, confidence and a lifelong love of learning.
Our curriculum ensures strong foundations in English and mathematics, while also providing rich learning opportunities across the wider curriculum including science, humanities, the arts, computing and physical education.
As a single-form entry school, teachers know pupils well and are able to support each child’s learning and progress effectively.
Our most recent Ofsted inspection (March 2022) recognised the strength of the curriculum, noting that “the core subjects are of high quality” and that leaders are “crystal clear about what teachers need to do.”
Learning is enriched through a range of opportunities including school trips, themed learning days, clubs and sporting activities which help children develop confidence, creativity and independence.
Further information about each subject area can be found in the documents and curriculum information below.
We hold three parent consultation evenings each year to discuss progress and achievements and provide a small written report three times a year.

pageCache.pageTitle: Valley Road Primary School - House System
pageCache.text:
House System
At Valley Road School we operate a House System. All the children are allocated a House and they will spend all their time with us in that one House.
Children can earn House Points for their Houses by working hard in class, producing really good quality work, being polite and courteous, helping each other and by setting a good example.
As well as the academic side of school life, children also represent their Houses in Sports Day and other sporting/competitive events throughout the year.
The four Houses are:
Golden Eagles
Green Woodpeckers
Red Kites
Blue Kingfishers

pageCache.text:
About our school
Welcome to Valley Road School
Valley Road is a small, friendly primary school situated at the top of Henley-on-Thames in a safe and peaceful setting. As a single-form entry school, we are able to know every child as an individual while still offering a rich curriculum and a wide range of opportunities.
In March 2022, Ofsted described Valley Road as a place where “caring relationships lie at the heart” of the school and where pupils are “eloquent and zestful” learners who enjoy their education.
Valley Road has also received national recognition, being rated “Very Good” by The Telegraph 2025 and the only Henley primary school included in The Guardian’s nationwide ‘Top 200 Primary Schools’ 2025 list.
We are very proud of our school community and warmly welcome prospective families to visit and experience Valley Road for themselves.
If you would like to read the full Ofsted report, please click here. You can also view the school’s achievement and progress tables on the Department for Education website here.
If there is something you cannot find on our website, please do get in touch and we will be happy to help.
Our School
About our school

Admissions
Valley Road Primary School welcomes applications from families both within Henley-on-Thames and the surrounding area.
Administration of admission arrangements to County Primary Schools is dealt with centrally by Oxfordshire County Council. Full details of the application process, deadlines and admission criteria can be found on the Oxfordshire County Council website.
We encourage prospective parents to visit the school before applying. A visit provides the opportunity to see our classrooms, meet our staff and experience the warm and friendly atmosphere that makes Valley Road such a special place to learn.
Joining the school later on
Sometimes children join the school later on in their school life. We make every effort to ensure they are welcomed, looked after, and monitored so that they quickly make friends and can find their way around the school.
Teachers give children time to settle in before making an assessment of their academic abilities. This assessment, together with records from the previous school, will enable your child to have the best start in our school.

British Values
At Valley Road School, we value the diversity of the backgrounds of all pupils, families and the wider school community and strongly believe in upholding British Values through all aspects of our school provision.
We actively take opportunities to teach British values and feel this is embedded through our regular assemblies and interwoven in our enriching curriculum.
We explore the 5 areas of British Values as part of our curriculum:
We aim to nurture our children on their journey through life so they can grow into safe, caring, democratic, responsible and tolerant adults who make a positive difference to British society and to the world and the wider world.

PTA
The Valley Road PTA was granted charitable status in 1999 and is now a registered charity. There are five Trustees who are elected annually.
The aim of the PTA is to encourage the active interest of parents and friends in the life of the school and to raise money for school funds, including the recently launched Gift Aid Scheme. All parents are automatically members of the Association and are eligible to vote at the Annual General Meeting which is held in the Summer Term.
Throughout the year, the PTA arranges a number of social and fundraising events. The children benefit greatly from the extra equipment, books and subsidies that are financed from the Association’s funds. The school minibus, which is used by all the children, was purchased by the PTA and continues to be maintained from the same source.
The present chairs of the PTA are Natalie Postlethwaite and Victoria Montgomery.
Our School

Safeguarding
Safeguarding the welfare of our pupils is our highest priority at Valley Road Primary School.
We are committed to ensuring that every child feels safe, supported and able to learn in a secure environment. All staff receive regular safeguarding training and follow the school’s safeguarding and child protection procedures.
Our most recent Ofsted inspection (March 2022) confirmed that safeguarding arrangements at Valley Road are effective and that leaders ensure pupils feel safe at school.
If you have any concerns about a child’s safety or wellbeing, please contact one of the school’s Designated Safeguarding Leads: Mrs Gemma Sterjo Mrs Nicola Gordon
Further information can be found in the school’s Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy.

Sports
Our aim at Valley Road School is to provide the opportunity for our children to safely experience a range of sporting activities for their fun and enjoyment.
Through carefully planned PE and sports activities we aim to ensure that all children are happy and enjoy PE, thus raising participation levels both in and out of school and therefore in turn, promoting healthy lifestyles.
We strive to provide high-quality PE and sports teaching in both curriculum and after school clubs. We aim to ensure that within their own level of ability all children can achieve and experience success, thereby enabling them to reach their full potential.
We value the benefits of PE and sport to build children’s self-confidence, esteem and self-worth which is character-building and essential for our pupil’s development.
We aim to teach children the skills necessary when taking part in a variety of different sports and how this can be transferred in other subjects across the curriculum, so all children become more active as this will support progress in all other subjects.
